title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention and timeouts
author: Ava Thompson
description: Context: the continuous-batcher scheduler has been observed in mixed-priority workloads to favor high-throughput low-latency paths and starve lower-priority/long-running requests, occasionally causing request timeouts and poor fairness at scale. Motivation: reduce starvation and provide deterministic timeout enforcement without regressing throughput or latency for common RL/QA workloads. Changes: 1) introduce per-priority aging queues that track enqueue time and escalate requests after an age threshold; 2) add configurable soft and hard timeouts for queueing and in-flight execution with metrics and enforceable cancellation; 3) implement weighted round-robin admission across priority buckets with dynamic weight decay when a class is starved; 4) add a compact timeout wheel for O(1) timer checks to avoid GC spikes; 5) expose three new knobs in config: queue_age_threshold_ms, per_priority_weight, and timeout_enforcement_mode (none/soft/hard). Benchmarks: microbench + end-to-end load tests show P95 tail for mixed-priority workload reduced by ~18% and worst-case queue drop rate eliminated in stress tests. Backcompat: default config preserves previous behavior (timeouts disabled) and feature is gated behind an opt-in config flag. Rollout: staged canary on Dedicated clusters, ramp to 25% then 100% over 48h with automatic rollback if P95 latency worsens >10% or error rate increases >0.5%. Testing: unit tests for scheduler invariants, integration-load harness, and chaos test to verify starvation prevention under preemption. Notes: documented config and telemetry in the console; added migration note for Private installer (config schema bump).

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Can you explain how the age threshold interacts with batching (does aging force immediate batch flush?)?

Ava Thompson: Aging marks requests as high-priority for admission but does not force a flush; it is a hint to scheduler to prefer the aged request in the next admission window. Added comment and unit test to clarify behavior.
Rina Patel: We need metrics to detect thrashing when weights change dynamically.
Ava Thompson: Added scheduler_aging_{avg,p95} and a decay-rate metric; included in dashboard JSON and integration checks.
Samir Gupta: Please ensure timeouts are safe for Private clusters where customers may disable timeouts.
Ava Thompson: Default is timeout_enforcement_mode=none; added helm/value flags and docs; added e2e test that verifies default behavior remains unchanged.
Rina Patel: Approve after adding the integration load test results and CI green.
release_notes: runtime: continuous-batcher scheduler tuned to prevent starvation and enforce queue/in-flight timeouts (opt-in). Improves fairness across priority classes and reduces P95 tail latency for mixed workloads.
rollout_plan: Canary on Dedicated: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h with automated rollback if P95 latency increases >10% or error rate >0.5%. Private installers: config schema bump, documented migration steps.
